### y1v1 p.14-15 — Opening monologue: equality is a lie (Ch.1)
[scene] direct address to the reader before the story opens; not a character scene
[narrates] (p.14) "I know this is kind of sudden, but, please, it will only take a moment. I want your honest opinion."
[narrates] (p.14) "Are people equal or not?"
[narrates] (p.14) "A proper society will constantly strive for equality. There are those who clamor for men and women to always be considered equal. As a result, we raised the employment rate for women, we made specialized subway cars only for women. Sometimes, women will even argue over the order of names in a family register. The public opinion of people with disabilities has also changed. We’re now told that we should not use the term “disabled people” when referring to them, so as not to discriminate. Nowadays, children are taught that all people are created equal."
[narrates] (p.14) "But is that true? I have my doubts. If men and women have different abilities, then their roles should also differ. People with disabilities are still disabled, no matter what polite euphemisms you use. No matter how you try to avert your eyes, the meaning of the word does not change."
[narrates] (p.14) "So, my answer would be, “No, we are not equal.” To be human is to be unequal. Equality does not exist."
[narrates] (p.14) "Long ago, in a bygone era, a great man said that heaven does not set one man above or below any other. However, he did not necessarily adhere to the idea that everyone is equal. Did you know that there is more to that famous passage? The rest goes like this: Everyone is equal when they are born, so I ask, why do we see differences in position and status? And it continues: Do you or do you not encourage learning to create a difference?"
[narrates] (p.14) "So then, education creates an imbalance. The point’s spelled out there, in the incredibly famous work Gakumon no Sume. Even though this is the year 2015, the modern era, nothing about these teachings has changed. The situation has only grown more complex and fraught."
[narrates] (p.14) "In any case, we are human beings. We are living, thinking creatures."
[narrates] (p.15) "I don’t think it right to simply say that we are unequal and then live our lives based on pure instinct. In other words, though “equality” is a complete lie, we cannot accept inequality, either. Right now, I’m trying to come up with a new answer for humanity’s eternal question."
[narrates] (p.15) "Hey, you there. You, the one reading this book right now. Have you ever given serious thought to the future?"
[narrates] (p.15) "Have you ever considered the purpose of going to high school or to college? Though the future may seem hazy right now, do you think you’ll find a job someday? That’s what I used to think. Back when I finished my compulsory education and became a high school student, I hadn’t really considered the future. I’d only felt joy at being nearly free of obligation. I didn’t consider the incredible influence that school would continue to have in my life, on my future. I didn’t even understand the purpose behind studying language or numbers."
[trait] philosophical, contrarian on equality; frames the self as a detached analyst

[says] (p.59) The perpetrator lecture to Kushida: "I understand a little of what Horikita meant. At the very least, Sudou does share some fault in this case. He’s the type who gets angry easily, right? Whenever he’s faced with someone he doesn’t like, he lashes out, and speaks and acts in an aggressive, domineering way. When I heard he was being considered for a regular spot on the basketball team, I was both surprised and impressed. No one disagrees that he’s an incredible player, but if he acts so arrogant and prideful, some people will come to hate him. Those who work incredibly hard for their spot would probably see Sudou as a rather disagreeable person. Then there are the rumors, right? People say that Sudou’s been fighting people since junior high. I haven’t met anyone who knew Sudou at his previous school, but considering how many people are talking about it, there might be something to the rumor."
[says] (p.59) "This was bound to happen eventually. That’s why Horikita said Sudou was a perpetrator."
[says] (p.59) "Yeah. As long as he continues to antagonize those around him, trouble will inevitably follow. Also, if there’s no proof, then people will use his image against him. In other words, they’ll judge him based on their impressions. For example, let’s say there was a murder case. There are two suspects. One of them has committed murder in the past, while the other is a good, upstanding citizen. Based on that information, who would you believe?"
[says] (p.59) "The truth might be different. However, the less information you have upon which to base your judgment, the more you have to rely on whatever meager information you have at hand. That’s what’s happening here. Horikita cannot overlook the fact that Sudou doesn’t recognize his flaws."
[thinks] (p.60) "I didn’t think this was exactly a 'you reap what you sow' situation, though."
[says] (p.60) "I guess so, yeah. By punishing him, she wants him to understand himself better."
[says] (p.60) "You should act according to your own principles, Kushida. I don’t think it’s wrong to want to help Sudou."
[says] (p.60) "However, I think it would be better if we carefully considered whether or not to directly point out Sudou’s problems. If he doesn’t actually take the time to reflect, there’s no point. There are certain realizations you can only come to on your own."
[feat] (p.60) "Kushida arched her back and stretched; I’d changed her thinking." — influence over the class's social engine, exercised quietly and without credit.
[says] (p.61) "If no one has any objections, how about we start by asking around Class B?"
[says] (p.61) "Because that’s the class that would most want a witness."
[says] (p.61) "Between D and C, which class most threatens Class B? Or to put it another way, which class is more likely to threaten B’s place in the ranking?"
[says] (p.61) "We know too little about Class A. I don’t think they’d want to get involved in a troublesome affair that might negatively impact their points. It's also possible that Class A students don’t care, as they feel no connection to what goes on between C and D."
[thinks] (p.61) Caution about B: "If they had a particularly cunning person, he or she might have devised a plan to defeat not only C, but Class D as well."
[says] (p.61) "Stop." (reflexively grabbing Kushida's collar to halt her charge)
[says] (p.62) "It is certainly true that your excellent communication skills are indispensable. However, this isn’t the same as casually strolling into another class and trying to make friends."
[says] (p.62) "Do you know anyone in Class B?" → "Well then, let’s talk to those people first then."
[says] (p.62) "I see. You might be right about that. We should do what you think is best, Kushida." (concedes the one-by-one vs group-ask debate)
[trait] (p.62) "Suddenly, I felt a sensation, like someone was watching me. I turned around." — watched-sense in a one-third-empty classroom; unresolved in-chapter.
[thinks] (p.61) "So cuuute!" reaction: "She was probably being adorable on purpose… Despite thinking that, my heart pounded like crazy."
[says] (p.64) "I wanna go home." (grumbling at the window during the Class B visit)
[says] (p.64) "You’re probably right," (to Ike's anti-club rant — agreeing while internally cataloguing club benefits: "You gained the skills necessary to build relationships with other people, and you also got to experience victory and defeat.")
[thinks] (p.64) "I waited for a few minutes until I received Kushida’s report. I certainly didn’t expect what she told me." — chapter-ending hook into Ch.4.
[rel:kushida-kikyou] (p.54–62) She commands his schedule by asking nicely; he concedes plans to her judgment while supplying the strategy; collar-grab intimacy registers as both protectiveness and fluster.

### y1v2 p.66–74 — Ch.4 sec. 4.0–4.1: the class-change rule, and the mean-teacher read
[thinks] (p.66) On the search's division of labour: "Meanwhile, I was alone, like always. I could talk to Kushida, but felt disadvantaged when it came to a big group. I couldn’t really talk, so I asked Kushida to fill in me later."
[thinks] (p.67) The only witness to Horikita's contempt for the grievance session: "As her neighbor, I was the only one who noticed." — and on her book: "At a glance, I saw she was reading Dostoevsky’s Demons. A good choice."
[rule] (p.68) He is one of two who can authenticate the class-change claim, and he reads the teacher's glance: "Chabashira-sensei shot a quick glance over at Horikita and me. We had tested out that very method ourselves by buying a test point from the school."
[thinks] (p.68) His prior on the teacher, stated as a rule of the school: "Chabashira-sensei sometimes withheld information, but she didn’t lie."
[thinks] (p.71) His verdict on the club-points reveal: "At any rate, I deduced that our homeroom teacher was being extremely and deliberately mean." — followed by an even-handed note on Ike's side: "If someone were to join a club simply for the sake of earning points, he or she probably wouldn’t see great results... On the other hand, someone who joined the club for the sake of points might discover that they possessed a talent for it."
[says] (p.72) "Horikita. Doesn’t this mean there’s some value in saving Sudou?" — the argument he chooses to make when he decides to move her: points, not feeling.
[says] (p.72) "It’s better to have a lot of private points, right? He can supplement his own grade if he fails, and he can save others."
[thinks] (p.72) "Whether class points or private points, it was better to have a lot of them. There were absolutely no negatives to that. Also, we knew very little about how else to earn points at this stage. If our chances improved with Sudou in the class, then that was reason enough to make an effort."
[scene] (p.73) He stops the moment she concedes: "I considered it unnecessary to say more, so I stopped talking. Horikita pondered the issue in silence."
[thinks] (p.74) His self-assessment on the canvassing: "I hung behind Kushida, Ike, and the others, trailing them like a ghost. I was impressed, surprised, and in awe of their natural conversation skills... How could they talk with people they’d never met before and behave like old friends? Monsters."
[thinks] (p.74) On Horikita's refusal of Kushida's invitations, which he watches daily: "my neighbor—who continued to reject Kushida’s invitations, no matter what—sat with a nonchalant expression as she prepared for class."

### y1v2 p.75–82 — Ch.4 sec. 4.1: Horikita names the witness, and he cannot place her either
[scene] (p.75) He notices the game Sudou is playing while the meeting works: "the person of interest, Sudou, was completely engrossed in some kind of digital basketball game on his phone... I think the game was called Generation of Miracles or something, but I still didn’t quite understand."
[thinks] (p.77) "She spoke as if she had already found the hypothetical witness." — and the room's verdict on it: "No one, myself included, really believed her…until we heard her next words."
[limit] (p.77) Horikita's observation beats his own, and he says so plainly: "I hadn’t noticed that at all. I was genuinely impressed by Horikita’s observational prowess."
[says] (p.78) Horikita's jab at him lands by name: "Since you were one of the people who also stares at Kushida-san, it’s not surprising you didn’t notice."
[says] (p.79) His own contribution to identifying Sakura is a memory of a name only: "I probably know her. I feel like I’ve heard her name somewhere before," — "I felt like I almost had something, but not quite."
[thinks] (p.80) On being lumped in with the boys' appraisal of Sakura's body without having said anything: "Even though I hadn’t said anything, I felt like I was being lumped into the same category as Ike and Yamauchi. Kushida’s bitter smile seemed to say, You’re also fixated on boobs, aren’t you? You disgusting pervert. Granted, that was my persecution complex speaking."
[thinks] (p.82) "I could barely match Sakura’s name to a face. I recalled seeing her back when we were making bets. The bet had been about boobs, though. I guess we were birds of a feather after all."
[scene] (p.85) His taxonomy of the class's four kinds of solitude, with himself as a category: "Kushida and Hirata were proactive and able to open up to just about anyone. Horikita didn’t feel the agony of solitude. So what about Sakura? Did she like being alone, like Horikita? Or was she suffering because she didn’t know how to connect with people, like me?"

### y1v2 p.86–96 — Ch.4 sec. 4.2–4.3: the theory of personal space, and the cameras he had already found
[feat] (p.88) He diagnoses Kushida's failure analytically, in the middle of an awkward conversation, by citing a discipline: "Cultural anthropologist Edward Hall further divided the idea of personal space into four parts. [thinks] (p.88) What he notices about Sakura's body that nobody else in the room reports: "Sakura concealed her dominant hand while also avoiding eye contact. Even if she weren’t comfortable meeting someone’s eyes, people generally looked in the direction of those to whom they were speaking."
[thinks] (p.88) His own reading of Kushida's one-to-one manner, held alongside the class's: "Though it was mostly out of formal obligation, Sakura had exchanged numbers with Kushida. I’d found something a bit off-putting about it myself."
[says] (p.90–91) "I don’t think self-defense is all that helpful in this case." — AK: "Ah, I’d accidentally said that aloud." The slip is the same conclusion he gave Sudou privately in Ch.2 (p.33), said now without choosing to.
[scene] (p.91) Kushida invades his space to ask for his loyalty and he catalogues his own reaction instead: "Man, Kushida looked super cute up close. Rather than feeling uncomfortable about this invasion of my personal space, I wanted her to come even closer."

[thinks] (p.91) "If even Sakura, the key witness, denied Sudou her help, then we’d made no progress."
[says] (p.94) "There’s a popular expression in this world: Great talents mature late. Sudou could probably become a professional player in the NBA, right? I think there’s a possibility that he’ll make a great contribution to society. The power of youth is infinite." — his own verdict on the performance: "I uttered a catchphrase that sounded about as original as a television commercial."
[thinks] (p.95) His discovery of the classroom cameras and the reason no one else saw them: "Well, ordinary people don’t typically concern themselves with hidden cameras... Or they might have accidentally spotted them."
[scene] (p.95–96) Horikita asks him to walk back and he touches her forehead first: "After hearing that invitation, I reflexively placed my hand against her forehead. It felt nice and cool, but I noticed the softness of her skin." — "It was rare for Horikita to invite me anywhere. With the world going so topsy-turvy, I wondered if it would rain tomorrow."
[rel:hirata-yousuke] (p.83–84) Hirata briefs him on the witness for Horikita-relay reasons, and invites him to hang out with the couple; AK's interior reaction is the volume's most explicit record of wanting to be included: "Hirata smiled, agreeably. [says] (p.97) "I decided to take some initiative by myself, since I’m not very good at interacting with Hirata, Kushida, or large groups of people. Being social’s definitely not my forte. [says] (p.99) "Of course I haven’t. It’s your job to come up with plans, Horikita. I won’t ask you to save Sudou, but it’d be nice for you to point Class D in the right direction."
[thinks] (p.99) His read of Horikita's candor, and of everyone else's: "most people aren’t suited for loneliness. Therefore, they sometimes behave hypocritically, like saving someone out of feigned altruism in order to make other people adore them. That didn’t seem to be Horikita’s style, though."
[thinks] (p.100) The case in one line, as he states it to himself at the scene: "One party, either Sudou or the Class C students, had summoned the other to the special building. [says] (p.102) "You shouldn’t feel obligated to appear as the witness, Sakura. It’d be pointless to force you to testify. [thinks] (p.102) "Are you talking about me?" Horikita muttered — "Ignoring the existence of such a scary monster, I decided to let Sakura go."

[thinks] (p.102) How much Horikita's certainty is worth: "So far, we’d been operating based purely on Horikita’s dogmatism and prejudices. It was quite possible that Sakura wasn’t the witness, like she said."

[thinks] (p.106) His running account of Ichinose's offer: "Obviously, I couldn’t trust Ichinose yet. She was a student from Class B, and she gained nothing by involving herself. [thinks] (p.106) On who decides: "I glanced over to see what Horikita thought... I didn’t really have the power to decide in the first place; that was Horikita’s job."
[status] (p.107) The information gap is now his explicit grievance against the school: "This was yet another oversight, another instance where Chabashira-sensei had failed to disclose something important... ### y1v2 p.123–127 — Ch.4 sec. 4.7: he refuses to be the lie in someone else's confession
[says] (p.123) "So, what should I do next?"
[thinks] (p.123) "No way… Did Ichinose plan to confess to me?!" — the misread the section is built on, corrected in the next line by her "I think someone will confess their feelings to me here".
[says] (p.124) "Wouldn’t it be better if I weren’t here?"
[says] (p.124) "I don’t really think I’m the person to ask for this. I don’t have any experience with romantic confessions. There are probably other people in Class B who could help."
[says] (p.124) "But Ichinose, aren’t you used to people confessing their feelings to you?"
[says] (p.124) "I understand that you don’t want to hurt anyone, but won’t it be worse if they find out you lied?"
[says] (p.125) "Honestly, I think it would be much better for you to talk with this person one-on-one. Truthfully."
[says] (p.126) "I’m just a friend." — "I cut Ichinose off before she could finish."

Don’t you think you should answer someone when they desperately long to express their feelings? If you make the situation unclear, both of you may regret it later."
[thinks] (p.126) "Trying to prevent someone’s pain was useless. If you turned someone down, their feelings would inevitably be hurt." and then "Even more hurt if the excuse were built on a lie."

[trait] (p.126–127) The one extended piece of sincere moral advice he gives all volume is about someone else's confession, delivered to a girl who did not ask for it, and followed by walking away before the answer arrives.

### y1v3 p.13–23 — Ch.2 sec. 2.0: the cruise, the first-name fever, and the boundary
[scene] (p.13) Deck of the luxury liner on the way to the school's private island; first-years of Class D around him after midterms and finals.
[narrates] (p.13) The chapter is his first-person account: "The endless summer sea. The infinite blue skies. The perfectly clear air."
[thinks] (p.14) Prices the trip honestly: on his own it "would probably have cost me about 100,000 yen, even in the off season."
[action] (p.15) Shoved by a Class A boy ("Hey, you're in the way. Move it, you defects.") and catches the railing; Sudou answers back, Class D is chased from the bow.
[trait] (p.15) Reads the hierarchy and swallows it: "Although the situation was unfair, we didn't need any unnecessary trouble, so it was best to ignore it."
[thinks] (p.16) Notes Hirata's arrival as rescue: "I was saved by the appearance of my hero, Hirata Man."
[thinks] (p.16) On Hirata and Karuizawa cooling off: "They seemed to get along well whenever I saw them talking."

[says] (p.211) “You think there are signs of that with Hirata?”
[says:sudou-ken] (p.211) “Well, saying he’s gonna have a breakdown would be an exaggeration, but I think there’s danger there.”

### y1v3 p.226–227 — Ch.6 sec. 6.10: the footprints

### y1v3 p.229–235 — Ch.6 sec. 6.10: carrying Horikita
[scene] (p.229) She wakes in his arms under a tree, fever high, and the night turns on the choice between carrying on and retiring.

[says] (p.230) “It’s just that you’ve started to sound like you need allies.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.230) “I should have understood this a long time ago…”
[says] (p.230) “Don’t talk. You’re sick.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.231) “I’m going to try to get up to Class A using my own abilities. I’ll definitely recover from this failure…”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.231) “I’m prepared to be hated by everyone else… This was all my mistake.”
[says] (p.231) “According to this school’s system, if you fight by yourself, you won’t reach Class A. We need to cooperate with our classmates. It’s unavoidable.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.231) “I can’t accept that. No matter how hard it is, I’m still…alone.”
[says] (p.231) “Ah, shut up already! Stop talking. Right now, you won’t be able to convince anyone.”
[action] (p.231) Embraces her tightly as she talks of her dream.
[says] (p.231) “You can’t bear every responsibility. You’re not that strong, unfortunately.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.231) “So you’re telling me to give up? I have a dream to reach Class A, a dream for my brother to acknowledge me.”
[says] (p.231) “No one said you have to give up.”
[says] (p.231) “If you can’t fight by yourself, it’s better to fight with a partner. I’ll lend you a hand.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.231) “Why? You’re not the kind of person who would say such things…”
[says] (p.231) “Well, why then? I wonder.”

[action] (p.232) Takes the wrong route, slips on the collapsed soil, and curls around her to shield the fall down the slope.
[action] (p.232) Shelters under an overgrown tree with her head in his lap while the fever burns.
[says] (p.233) “It’s already almost six o’clock, Horikita. You might think this will sound harsh, but you should retire. Your body is probably at its limit.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.233) “I can’t do that. We can’t afford to lose thirty points because of me… I was the one who confronted Karuizawa-san and the others about using points, right? It would make me look like such an idiot…”

[says] (p.233) “Class D will lose another fifty points.”

[says] (p.233) “What are you planning to do?”

[says] (p.233) “Things aren’t that easy. You’re feeling really weak now, and our teacher isn’t kind enough to let you act your way past her. It will be impossible for you to get back to camp on your own.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.234) “Yes. That’s the correct decision. Everything was my responsibility.”

[says] (p.234) “Can you really make it back alone by tomorrow morning?”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.234) “I failed due to my negligence. That’s all.”
[says] (p.234) “You’re wrong. You’re completely wrong.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.234) “Go… Because I think of you as my friend, please listen to my request…”

[thinks] (p.235) “I don’t care what I have to sacrifice. As long as I have my victory in the end, I’ll be fine.”
[thinks] (p.235) “You, Hirata—no, all other people are nothing more than tools. I was complicit in what drove you to this. So, don’t blame yourself, Horikita. You were useful to me.”
[note] (p.235) The monologue answers her friend line without ever being spoken to her.

### y1v3 p.237–238 — Ch.6 sec. 6.10: the ship at 7:58
[scene] (p.237) Reaches the ship at the pier with the storm still on, minutes before roll call.

[action] (p.237) A teacher stops him on the deck — “You’re prohibited from entering here. You’ll be disqualified.” — and he answers the emergency.
[says] (p.237) “This is an emergency. She’s got a high fever and has lost consciousness. Please let her rest right away.”

[action] (p.237) It is 7:58; the teacher answers — “You are certainly right. It is quite close. However, you’re out.”
[says] (p.237) “I understand. Oh, one more thing. I’d like to return this keycard.”
[action] (p.237) Hands over the key card and leaves the ship before the rain lets up.
[rule] (p.238) Class D loses thirty points to Horikita’s retirement and five more to his absence at roll call.

### y1v3 p.248–249 — Ch.7: the Icarus talk
[scene] (p.248) Chabashira intercepts him on the empty side of the ship and confirms, through the Icarus myth, that the man who demanded his expulsion is his father.
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.248) “May I have a word with you?”

[says] (p.248) “It’s hot, so please keep it brief.”
[says] (p.248) “Is it safe to say that for the time being, you’re satisfied?”
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.248) “Yes. First, I’d like to say that you did wonderfully. I’m honestly impressed.”
[says] (p.248) “Well, tell me something. Is it really true? Did he demand I be expelled from school?”
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.248) “Do you have any basis for saying that the story is true?”
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.248) “I know quite a lot about you. Might not that be the reason, more than anything else? Other teachers don’t know about your true abilities. But I have no doubts.”
[feat] (p.248) Claims knowledge of his true abilities that the other teachers do not have.
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.248) “I’m sure that you’ve heard of this rather famous myth, the wings of Icarus.”
[says] (p.248) “Why do you bring that up?” I asked.

It was because his father, Daedalus, had constructed wings and instructed him to fly. He didn’t fly because of his own intentions. Don’t you think that sounds exactly like your current predicament?”

[says:chabashira-sae] (p.249) “That man—no, your father—said this: ‘Sooner or later, Kiyotaka will gladly chase the means of his expulsion from school.’ You’re welcoming your end, much like how Icarus fell into the sea and died after his wings were burned, because he’d flown too close to the sun.”
[fact] (p.249) The man who demanded his expulsion from the school is named as his father, with the father’s own words quoted.
[says:chabashira-sae] (p.249) “So, what do you plan to do?” she asked.
[says] (p.249) “You should know, Sensei. Icarus won’t heed Daedalus’ warnings.”
[voice] (p.249) Answers her myth with the myth — burned wings and all, he flies on for his freedom.

### y1v3 p.250–258 — Ch.7 sec. 7.1: the whole explanation
[scene] (p.250) Section 7.1 opens with Horikita storming the lounge for the full story; he gives it on one condition — she never investigates him.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.250) “What do these test results mean? What in the world happened?”
[says] (p.250) “You look like you don’t have any idea at all.”
[note] (p.250) Untagged; it answers her question in his own viewpoint, so it is recorded as his.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.250) “I just can’t imagine it. I don’t understand it at all. I have a mountain of questions.”
[says] (p.250) “I’ll tell you everything. However, my one condition is that you stay quiet on this matter. I won’t compromise on this.”
[goal] (p.250) Sets the price of the story: her silence, with no compromise.
[says] (p.250) “What would you like to ask?”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.250) “What were you doing during the test? Tell me,” she said.
[says] (p.250) “When the special test was announced, I didn’t focus on anything except for the additional rules. I roughly understood how to manage the 300 points, but you couldn’t manipulate them as an individual.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.250) “But the additional rules were really difficult to understand. If you did things normally, you wouldn’t have been able to identify the leaders. Right?”
[says] (p.250) “Yeah. First of all, I volunteered to join the search for the base camp. Able to move freely, I planned to search out spot locations ahead of everyone else.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.251) “You make it sound simple, but no one should have known the spot locations.”
[says] (p.251) “That’s not true. You didn’t understand because you were ill and holed up inside the ship, but the school already gave us hints about the locations when we were sailing around the island.”
[fact] (p.251) The circling ship — nearly three times a usual cruise’s speed — and the phrase “significant scenery” were the school’s hints about the spot locations; Katsuragi and Kōenji had noticed the same hint.
[says] (p.251) “Then, I reached the cave. I thought it was the most important base.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.251) “The cave was the most important base? Don’t you think that the river and the well would have been more convenient, though?”
[says] (p.251) “The spot itself wasn’t what was important. Its location was.”

### y1v4.5 p.10 — Ch.1: the collection frame
[scene] (p.10) One-page first-person frame before the vignettes: no character appears and no school business is named — only the narrator’s case against end-of-summer melancholy.
[narrates] (p.10) “This is a selection of vignettes about students wavering in that space between childhood and adulthood.”
[trait] (p.10) The frame’s stance: refuses the end-of-vacation blues — the free years of life are the school years, and most of a life is spent sacrificing for society.
[note] (p.10) The page prints no name; read as the series narrator’s frame, following the first volume’s opening monologue.

### y2v1 p.44–49 — Exam rewards, rules, and the expulsion condition
[trivia] (p.44) Five subjects, 100 points each (500 total); class rewards 50/30/10/0 by average; individual rewards — top five pairs ¥100,000, top 30% ¥10,000.
[rule] (p.44) A pair scoring under 500 expels the second-year; the first-year loses private points for three months. Deliberately lowering scores (or forcing another to) expels the offender regardless of year.
[rule] (p.46) One partnership application per day via OAA; accept = final and irreversible (except expulsion/serious illness); profiles show results at 8:00 AM next day; partner identity not listed.
[rule] (p.47) Unpaired students get a random partner at 8:00 AM on exam day but suffer a 5% score penalty; the three leftover first-years (from three second-year expulsions) have scores doubled with the same 5% penalty.
[inference] (p.48–49) Analyzes that his own expulsion is certain unless his partner scores at least 1 point — even with his own full marks, a partner's zero dooms him; the anti-throwing rule is "indispensable" to legitimize the exam and protect average students.
[trait] (p.44–49) Recognizes this is an "exceedingly difficult" exam for him specifically; notes the rules make blatant misbehavior impossible.

[trait] (p.50) Notes his own OAA Academic Ability is a C — he can't freely choose a partner, and must avoid the White Room student who may be "lying in wait" for someone with a similar rating; judges this "more challenging than any other special exam."

### y2v12 p.12–19 — Ch.1: The announcement
[scene] (p.12) The second week of March, Thursday. Chabashira-sensei, our homeroom teacher, appears with a calm demeanor; the announcement the class has waited days for finally comes, prefaced by a personal story about her eighth year at the school.

### y2v12 p.69–76 — Ch.3: The rules drop
[scene] (p.69–70) Monitor reveals the representatives and match order: Class A (Sanada v, Kitō m, Sakayanagi g), Class B (Hirata v, Horikita m, Ayanokōji g), Class C (Nishino v, Katsuragi m, Ryūen g), Class D (Hamaguchi v, Kanzaki m, Ichinose g); venue classroom with 2 monitors/2 desks/tablets each; B vs D identical setup next door; the exam resembles the luxury cruise exam (Werewolf-type).
[rule] (p.70) Exam structure: reps select 5 groups of 7 participants by rotation; no consecutive group use; fewer than 35 → reuse allowed; each round 5 minutes; after each round each rep nominates one participant with a guessed role; correct ID shifts lives (honor student −3, mis-ID costs lives, etc.); discussion ends when all ordinary or all honor students leave; 5000 private points to survivors.
[rule] (p.72) Roles: honor students (2), teacher (1), graduate (1), underclassman (1), upperclassman (1), ordinary students (6-8), traitor (0-2 per class, one per exam); honor student correct ID costs opponent 3 lives; teacher/graduate successful ID 2 lives, executes role powers (teacher may block one nomination per game; graduate may learn one role per round but never a traitor).
[rule] (p.73) Leader eliminated is not replaced; general zero lives loses; both zero → rematch one-life-each; participants failing to attend lose; 50,000-pt rewards for teacher/graduate leftovers; traitors 5M pts or 50 class points if they survive; ordinary-side win → 10,000 pts each.
[scene] (p.71–76) He digests the mechanics: it's a social-deduction game; the win is measured in pressure-tested relationships; physical and academic ability are near-irrelevant; reps may watch only; discussion is watched 14-player; honor students call the shots on eliminations; traitors wreck predictions.
[note] (p.70–76) The design is deliberate: classes with deeper bonds and keener readers win; he recognizes the game instantly as a scaled-down sibling of the island/cruise exams.

### y3v3 p.17–20 — Disembarkation: the grid, Nakanishi's absence and the rules begin
[scene] (p.17) Disembarks onto the beach; the island is more developed than last year and cardboard boxes are stacked up.
[narrates] (p.17) A school official directs the third-years to line up by class at their homeroom teachers; no first- or second-years are landing yet.
[says] (p.17) "I remember quite a bit. Talk about nostalgia."

[thinks] (p.18) Nakanishi's absence was touched on lightly with no heavy penalty; since it is Ichinose's class and he is not a standout, the damage is likely minimal — the downside is real but small.
[narrates] (p.18) The island grid has been subdivided: last year A–J × 1–10, this year A–O × 1–15.
[narrates] (p.18) Exam duration is a maximum of three nights and four days, ending early on a decisive result; daily hours 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. (4:00 p.m. on the final day).
[narrates] (p.18) Five mandatory roles: Commander ×1 (GPS tablet, tactics, cannot be eliminated, confined to HQ F14), VIP ×3, plus Guards, Analysts ×2 and Scout ×1; the exam is won by eliminating other classes' VIPs and guards with paint guns.

### y3v3 p.21–24 — Tactics, watches, events and the expulsion penalty
[scene] (p.21) On the beach, Mashima-sensei explains that handling assigned roles and the commander's limited-use tactics will be critical.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.21) "Anyone here ever played a survival game? Or know anything about it?"
[narrates] (p.21) No one in Class C admits to knowing survival games, while Class A's Onizuka and Ijuuin chat excitedly, suggesting prior experience.
[narrates] (p.21) Commander tactics: Global GPS Shutdown (30 min, ×1), Individual GPS Shutdown (30 min, ×3), Identity Check (reveals name and role at a location, ×5); the using commander can still see positions every five minutes.
[thinks] (p.22) The global GPS shutdown in particular could be a trump card for surprise attacks or escaping pursuers, but poor timing would waste it.
[narrates] (p.22) Wristwatches are distributed and must be worn 24 hours a day; removal risks disqualification. The watch shows vitals, area and direction, and issues an "Out" when a paintball bursts on the sensor clothes.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.22) "An expulsion from the class whose three VIP's get taken out first, huh? Well, I figured they'd pull something like that."
[says] (p.22) "Is this what you expected?"
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.22) "Well, pretty much—"
[thinks] (p.24) The expulsion can be minimized — a class can nominate a student with Protection Points — but fear of it could produce a draw, and since a draw is decided by luck, no class can keep running; combat is forced.

### y3v3 p.25–28 — Weapons: the prototype paintball guns
[scene] (p.25) Mashima-sensei unveils the guards' weapons — assault rifles, shotguns, submachine guns and handguns — and Kishinami of Kanto Shooter Co. explains the prototype system.
[narrates] (p.25) The gym clothes incorporate proprietary temperature-sensitive, color-reacting and impact-sensor technology; a strong hit to the abdomen or back links to the watch and declares an out, while a tiny edge hit may not activate.
[narrates] (p.26) Self-reporting a malfunction-induced out avoids penalty, but continuing while knowing one is out is a serious violation that can cost the whole class the exam.
[thinks] (p.25) The lunchtime announcement and rules suggest the school is still going easy on them — an escape route far more lenient than expected.

### y3v3 p.29–30 — The starting-position lottery and meager supplies
[scene] (p.29) Mashima-sensei has one representative per class draw lots for the four starting areas — C12, E12, G12, I12 — about a 15-minute walk apart.
[thinks] (p.29) The western C12 (not sandwiched) and eastern I12 (easy to escape) look advantageous, but the result is the same whoever draws, so he has Sanada draw.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.29) "There were a lot of messy explanations, but basically, it means we just have to win a class vs class survival game, right?"
[says] (p.29) "Pretty much."
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.29) "For now, we keep our distance from the other classes and wait things out, yeah? Let's just have them crush each other."
[thinks] (p.29) That would be the most graceful outcome, but the rules are built so that anyone would want to reap the benefits of the chaos.
[narrates] (p.30) Class C starts at E12; Ryūen's B at C12, Horikita's A at G12, Ichinose's D at I12. Sanada apologizes for not drawing a corner area; Ayanokōji tells him not to worry.
[narrates] (p.30) Initial supplies are identical for every class and must be chosen now — leftovers are collected once the exam starts. The food is only two nutritional supplement blocks and mineral water per person, barely one lunch.
[thinks] (p.30) Securing food from event supplies becomes essential, which forces event participation and raises the risk of contact with other classes — clearly designed to induce combat.

### y3v3 p.33–35 — Tents and weapons: supplying the class
[scene] (p.33) The class sorts through the remaining boxes — small items, tents and weapons — and Ayanokōji sets a supply guideline.

[thinks] (p.33) He sets a framework first and folds in classmates' views later — the optimal way to avoid wasting time; favors two- and multi-person tents for shared carrying, since small tents become convenient as the class shrinks.
[narrates] (p.33) Forty main weapons are prepared — twenty assault rifles, ten submachine guns, ten shotguns — plus two handguns; each Guard can carry one main weapon.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.33) "They look real up close. This is my first time touching something like this."
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.33) "Man, the shotguns look hard to use, though. And they're heavy."
[thinks] (p.33) The assault rifle looks the most user-friendly and well-balanced; submachine guns and shotguns would only fill out the Guard ranks.
[says:morishita-ai] (p.34) "If we start with zero analysts, it looks like we can take two extra guns; what will you do?"
[says] (p.34) "Getting slightly more paintballs is certainly an advantage, but we will need analysts immediately. Considering the trouble of carrying and managing the guns at that time, it's hard to say if it's worth it."
[says] (p.34) "We'll go with a policy of not increasing our luggage."
[says:morishita-ai] (p.34) "So you don't intend to take any surplus. At times like this, human psychology makes us want to prepare at least a little insurance; one tends to get greedy."
[says] (p.34) "If we need something, we can just obtain it through an event. That's what the rules are for."

### y3v3 p.36–39 — Taking responsibility: I will be the one expelled
[scene] (p.36) The class reacts with horror to the idea of naming an expulsion sacrifice before the exam; Ayanokōji lets Morishita float Hashimoto's name, then intervenes.
[says] (p.37) "If Hashimoto is willing to volunteer, that's fine, but unfortunately, I have already decided who will be expelled, and I won't change it even if there are objections."
[says] (p.37) "If we end up receiving the penalty, I'll take on that role."
[says] (p.37) "Taking responsibility for defeat precisely because I am the leader. It sounds cool if I say it like that, but the reason is different. For better or worse, I'm an outsider. Not many days have gone by since I entered this class. If I, who joined to lead the class to victory, instead lead us to defeat, then bearing that responsibility is only logical."
[says] (p.37) "Either way, you wouldn't be able to trust a leader who lost miserably without being able to do anything, right?"
[says] (p.38) "As I just said, in the event that an expulsion occurs in the class, I want to confirm it's me. This is to prevent something like retracting it later. Announcing and determining it in advance is unrelated to the rules of the exam, right?"
[says] (p.38) "Of course. These aren't words that should be spoken merely to ease the anxiety of my classmates."
[thinks] (p.38) Without a firm public commitment he could resist at the last moment and shift the blame onto someone else — announcing it in advance removes that escape.
[inference] (p.37–38) The declaration is a calculated move to galvanize the class: it buys their trust and unites them behind him, while costing him nothing he intends to pay.
[trait] (p.36–39) Calm and strategically ruthless — deliberately lets the class squirm over the sacrifice before naming himself, knowing a leader who owns defeat is one they will follow.
[rel:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.36–38) Lets Morishita name him as sacrifice; Hashimoto is trapped into relying on Ayanokōji's ability since he has no other route to Class A.
[rel:morishita-ai] (p.36–38) Plays along with her proposal that Hashimoto be the victim.

### y0 p.131 — First memory: the pure white ceiling
[scene] (p.131) Recalls his very first memory in the White Room — staring at a pure white ceiling.
[narrates] (p.131) "The first memory everyone shared was of 'white' spreading across the entirety of the surface."
[narrates] (p.131) "As the name 'White Room' implied, this facility was based on the color white."
[narrates] (p.131) "The ceiling was no exception."
[narrates] (p.131) "In my first memory, I was staring at that pure white ceiling."
[narrates] (p.131) "Before showing interest in my own fingertips, I just wondered what this white ceiling was."
[narrates] (p.131) "Day after day, I just stared at the ceiling."
[narrates] (p.131) "At first, I cried, crying out of loneliness. Eventually, I learned that no one would come to help."
[trivia] (p.131) A newborn, unable to speak, accepted the environment as "the first lesson"; later he became aware of his fingers, sucking and licking them to pass empty time.
[trivia] (p.131) "Inhuman adults" brought only the nutrition necessary to live; even when sick, treatment was unemotional and life returned to normal — no one panicked, worried or rejoiced.
[trait] (p.131) Learned at an early stage that joy, anger, sorrow and pleasure were "practically useless" in the facility.

### y0 p.132–137 — The gummy hand-game at age two; the third option
[scene] (p.132) Recalls a one-on-one test at around age two — an instructor holds a tiny gummy in one hand.
[narrates] (p.132) "If you can guess where the gummy is, you can eat it."
[narrates] (p.132) "I'll keep giving you a chance to answer until you miss three times."
[trivia] (p.132) A tiny gummy — a rare snack in the facility, with a sweetness he craved; the instructor's face was stern, almost expressionless, and so was the two-year-old Kiyotaka's, naturally.
[trivia] (p.133) The first four rounds the gummy is in the right hand; the fifth the instructor crosses both arms behind his back, grip and position identical, gaze unchanged — a fifty-fifty choice; he touches the right, which is empty.
[trivia] (p.134) Other children had a slightly higher right-hand bias with "no clear reason"; all instructors actually held the gummies in their left hands that round.
[trivia] (p.134) He observes the other children's choices — an overwhelming number point left, but the answer is right — and infers the instructor's gummy is in the right; he points right and a green gummy appears.
[trivia] (p.134) The hands won't open until everyone has answered ("You're the last one"); everyone guesses wrong, and most children hit three misses and lose their chance.
[narrates] (p.135) "Why point behind?"
[narrates] (p.135) "Gummy, it's not there."
[trivia] (p.135) On his last chance he points behind (neither hand), reasoning the gummy might be hidden elsewhere; the instructor opens both hands — the gummy was in the right; the instructor eats it himself.
[narrates] (p.136) "Behind."
[trivia] (p.136) With a special extra chance, he again points behind; the gummy was in the left — "Too bad again. Are you frustrated?" He nods, frustrated not by wanting the gummy but by his thinking being off.
[inference] (p.136) The adults whisper that he — unlike the other children — observed others' choices, conceived a third option, and didn't discard it even after it was disproved; they remark it is not the thought process of a two-year-old, and argue over whether he understands them.
[trait] (p.132–137) Even at two, reasons by observation and inference rather than instinct — tracks others' behavior, considers hidden alternatives, and is driven by accuracy rather than reward.
[note] (p.137) When the buzzer ends the test, the adults leave and not a single child cries — being left alone with no help was deeply ingrained by age two.

### y0 p.138–139 — Names, no surnames; the written exam at four
[scene] (p.138) Recalls being told to state his name — "Kiyotaka" — a symbol, an identifying sequence of letters.
[narrates] (p.138) "Kiyotaka."
[trivia] (p.138) White Room children were taught names to identify people, but not surnames when young — instructors used first names, a rule set to prevent future identification.
[trivia] (p.138) By age four, new curriculums were implemented one after another; the written exam used hiragana, katakana, the alphabet, numbers and simple kanji, with pen-gripping fingers moving without hesitation.
[trivia] (p.138–139) A certain score within a time limit was required or there was a penalty; elegant handwriting was mandatory — no extra points for good handwriting, but hurried or poor handwriting meant deductions.
[trivia] (p.139) "No one in this facility asked whether the problems could be solved or not. The only answer was that everyone could do it"; those who couldn't were eliminated at age three.
[number] (p.139) The fourth generation initially numbered seventy-four; those judged incapable at three had already dropped out. The written exam lasted thirty minutes but strong students finished in half to two-thirds the time.

### y0 p.140–142 — Judo, randori, and Mikuru's collapse
[scene] (p.140) Recalls the judo curriculum added in their fourth year — being slammed to the floor by instructors, breathing knocked out, forced to stand.
[note] (p.140–141) The instructor shouts for them to get up, that he doesn't spare even children, and that no one will cry for them — the translation leaves these lines untagged, so no `[says]` row is claimed for them.
[trivia] (p.140) Judo had been learned for four months, progressing to randori (one-on-one sparring); the children were always made to taste bitter defeat against instructors.
[trivia] (p.140) Mikuru, pleading "I can't… stand anymore…!", clung to the instructor's leg, was shaken off, kicked away "spinning across the floor while scattering vomit around her," and lost consciousness; the instructor called her a "weakling" and had her removed.
[trivia] (p.141) The instructors were "the kind who wouldn't hesitate to push women and children to the brink of death"; being thrown, breathing difficulty and sobbing pain were normal, and even thinking about them a waste of energy.
[trivia] (p.142) After harsh lessons, they did randori with three other children at day's end; weak prey was hunted by the strong — a lesson learned. His record: 144 fights, 127 wins, 17 losses, currently a four-win streak.
[rel:mikuru] (p.140–141) Witnesses her brutal breakdown and removal.
[rel:shiro] (p.142) Faces him in randori — Shiro's record 135 wins, 9 losses, best at judo; waited and aimed for a counter this third fight.

### y0 p.149–150 — The daily schedule at age five
[scene] (p.149) Recalls the strict daily routine in the latter half of their fifth year.
[trivia] (p.149) 7:00 AM — an inorganic mechanical voice announces "Time to wake up," alarm exact to the second; staff remove the electrodes attached to them.
[trivia] (p.149) Immediate health check — height and weight changes; then bathroom; urine tests once a month and a small blood draw; staff leave without greetings.
[trivia] (p.149) Hydrate, thirty minutes of basic warmup training, record daily physical data such as grip strength, then training room with set quotas separated by gender — those who can't comply are barred from the room the next day.
[trivia] (p.149) By 8:00 AM — breakfast, nutrition-focused, evolved into supplements and nutrition blocks; taste and preference irrelevant, eaten in the order served.
[trivia] (p.150) Subjects: language arts, mathematics, economics, political science, with brief breaks until noon; similar lunch; studies at desks until 5:00 PM, then physical education; everything ends at 7:00 PM.
[trivia] (p.150) After dinner, bath and physical exam at 9:00 PM — a thirty-minute "meeting" for children only, no educators, to reflect on the day; topics not freely chosen, adults intervene only for "unnecessary chatter," silence permitted, conversations overheard — part of the curriculum with no assigned quota.
[trait] (p.149–150) Never spoke voluntarily in all this time; always just listened during the "meeting."

### y0 p.152–157 — Deliberately scoring 80 to keep the ceiling low
[scene] (p.152) Recalls the "thinning out" — as studies grew harder by two or three levels, children fell behind and were gradually removed.
[trivia] (p.152) The special high-difficulty exam's difficulty was set to the top score — a perfect score raised the ceiling and forced low scorers to struggle more next time; a sub-perfect top score lowered it.
[trivia] (p.153) Trivial calculation errors, careless oversights and excuses were unacceptable; children repeatedly checked papers even after finishing. He had already filled every answer and stared ahead, the questions and answers "etched word for word" in his mind.
[trivia] (p.154) He intentionally held back to score eighty points; an adult representative summoned him to a small private room after glancing at his paper.
[narrates] (p.154) "No."
[narrates] (p.154) "I wasn't instructed not to."
[narrates] (p.155) "In the first place, I've never once recognized the other children around me as comrades."
[narrates] (p.155) "It was more time-efficient to leave it blank."
[narrates] (p.155) "I won't make a mistake."
[narrates] (p.155) "If I hadn't held back, the percentage of children dropping out would have been much higher than it is now."
[narrates] (p.156) "No. Losing experience—that's how I thought of it."
[narrates] (p.156) "I want to know what the weak can see and feel."
[note] (p.154–156) The instructor's lines — calling his name, "it is foolish not to use the power you have," "leave the room," "why did you hold back," the accusation of camaraderie, and the warning that knowledge fades — are untagged in the corpus; no `[says]` row is claimed for them.
[inference] (p.152–156) He held back not from camaraderie (which he denies) but to gain data on weaker children and because writing answers he already knew was inefficient — a reason the instructors had never considered.
[trait] (p.156) Begins to dislike the instructor who lectures him; understands Yuki's aversion to carrots as a comparable irrational feeling.
[rel:suzukake-tanji] (p.156) Suzukake argues for observing him — "if he does something we hadn't even considered, that's exactly what we hoped for."
[rel:ishida-yuusuke] (p.156) Ishida is among the researchers who question his deliberate underperformance.
[note] (p.157) Another boy, sobbing, keeps writing after the buzzer and is dragged out screaming that he doesn't want to drop out, scattering gastric fluid over his paper, neck and clothes — though no one could drop out on that exam. Most children just stare ahead.

### y2v3 p.16–27 — The exam rules: points, watches, and twelve tables
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.16) "Starting tomorrow, your stay on the island will last for the next two weeks."
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.18) "The first three groups to arrive at area C8 will receive an 'Early Bird Bonus', with the first receiving 10 points, the second receiving 5 points, and the third receiving 3 points."
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.19) "should a group fail to reach a designated area three times in a row, they will lose one point."
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.24) "Starting tomorrow, all students will be required to wear one of these watches until the end of the exam."
[says:mashima-tomonari] (p.25) "the school will continuously monitor the wearer's body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen level, sleep cycle, stress levels, and so on."
[rule] (p.16–23) Groups of up to 6; bottom five groups face expulsion (nullifiable by points: 6M solo, 2M/person in a 3-group); points via "Basic Movement" to designated areas — Early Bird 10/5/3 + 1 Arrival per member; 4 areas/day (3 on first/last), one randomly placed; 3 consecutive misses cost points; one member reaching suffices (but Early Bird needs all).
[trivia] (p.23–27) All wear health-monitoring watches (Warning Alerts at abnormal metrics, Emergency Alert → 24h checkup or retirement, GPS summons staff after 5 min); watches can't be removed (points stop) and 12 different "Tables" assign each group different designated-area sequences so groups scatter.
[inference] (p.27) Considers Tsukishiro could tamper with his watch to make it malfunction and block his points — but only once or twice before it looks suspicious; as long as he stockpiles points he can avoid the bottom without competing for the top.
[rel:mashima-tomonari] (p.16–27) Delivers the exam briefing with Hoshinomiya; he listens critically, already factoring in sabotage.

[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.189) “That's a surprise. Naturally, I had already figured out which group each student in the class was assigned to when we got on the bus. I was just observing this time, so I didn't interfere with the exchange meeting.”

That's what you said. It's impossible for you to overlook Class A's group assignments, as you seem to pride yourself on. Yet, you didn't even mention Yamamura's name, did you?”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.190) “...Yes, that's right. I admit that I didn't mention Yamamura-san's name at that time. But it's none of your business, is it, Ayanokōji-kun?”

[says] (p.190) “You lost Kamuro. And at the same time, you were entrusted with her feelings. But that doesn't mean everything is back to normal. You haven't even finished choosing who to keep by your side, have you?”

[says] (p.190) “If you're still bothered by that, you should resolve it.”

[says] (p.190) “Strange?”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.190) “I thought you were just going to stand on the sidelines from now on. Isn't your unnecessary intervention excessive?”
[says] (p.190) “That's right. I also thought until a little while ago that I should just stand on the sidelines from here on.”
[says] (p.190) “I don't particularly want you to have anything to do with Yamamura. I don't have any such hopes at all. Whether you want to get closer or more distant, or even cut ties, is up to you. But if you're going to talk, now is the only time.”

[says] (p.190) “As I said earlier, I have Yamamura waiting in the dog park. She's been waiting for you in the cold for over 20 minutes now.”

[says] (p.191) “Then, just for now, I'll be your legs. That should make it easy for you to walk.”
[says:sakayanagi-arisu] (p.192) “...I'm sorry.”
[says] (p.192) “It's okay. It's my own meddling that started this.”

### y2v11 p.194–198 — Epilogue: The morning alone
[scene] (p.194) A few days after the exchange meeting; usual morning — but he leaves alone, 20 minutes early; soon February ends; Kei's problem waits; Ichinose's problem needs revisiting; one unexpected problem arose that wasn't in the plan.
[note] (p.194) “One problem arose that wasn't in the plan. That forced me to, in turn, make changes. There would be some negative effects as a result, but not all changes would be bad.” — the narration hints at an unnamed complication.
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.195) “You're early.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.195) “Good morning, Ayanokōji-kun.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.195) “In a way? That's a scary way to put it.”
[says] (p.195) “There's nothing to be wary of.”
[says] (p.195) “I wanted to have a meaningless conversation with you, unrelated to our interests.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.195) “Forever is an exaggeration. Sure, that's true, but we still have over a year until graduation, right? We don't have to arrange meetings like this, I can chat anytime.”
[says] (p.195) “What if I were to be expelled at the end-of-year exam?”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.196) “Then why don't you try to remember more common sense questions? You're good at studying.”

[says] (p.196) “That's reassuring.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.196) “Actually, I'm not worried about myself, but about the possibility of your expulsion.”
[says:horikita-suzune] (p.196) “In reality, that seems more likely.”

[says:horikita-suzune] (p.197) “Haha, you invited me to chat, but in the end, we're talking about the exam.”

### y2v11 p.199–204 — Epilogue: The betrayal Hashimoto hides
[scene] (p.199) Back to a few weeks earlier — when Hashimoto came to his room asking for help shortly before the exchange meeting; the night before everything.
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.199) “...Before I tell you what's next, there's something I really need to confirm with you.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.199) “I've been tempted to betray Ryūen since before the previous special exam. Not just temporarily teaming up, but moving classes based on that premise.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.199) “Of course, I didn't take such an invitation seriously at first. However, right after that, I heard from Ryūen that if I didn't move classes, I'd definitely regret it at the end of the school year.”
[says] (p.200) “Regret? Is it because Ryūen himself is confident that he'll win?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.200) “It seems that even you don't know about the content of the bet that Ryūen and Sakayanagi agreed on.”
[says] (p.200) “A bet, huh? I don't know if it applies, but I've heard a little about the exchange in the last deserted island exam. Unfortunately, I don't know the details.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “I'm glad. Then there was a reason for me to come here.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “It's not unreasonable to doubt the bet itself, right? No matter how you look at it, Sakayanagi is at a disadvantage.”
[says] (p.202) “That's true. However, Sakayanagi wouldn't choose to reject the bet just because of the disadvantage.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “Both are possible, but the details of the bet will eventually come to light. Considering that, it must be the latter. She must've allowed Ryūen to accumulate private points.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “Who else knows about this bet besides you and the parties involved?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “Unless Ryūen was lying, no one. You're the fourth. Well, both would hate to lose the bet by having it leaked.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “It took a while... for this day to come.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “Whether Sakayanagi wins or Ryūen wins, honestly, I couldn't make a judgment... No, I was kinda thinking that Sakayanagi might win.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “But even then, it's like 55 to 45. Seriously, it's not decisive, is it?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.202) “So I've been looking for a decisive factor, and what I thought that would be was—”
[says] (p.203) “Me?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.203) “If you were to follow Sakayanagi, I would've been ready to die with my current class without hesitation. That's why I advised Sakayanagi... to recruit you as an ally.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.203) “I will make Ryūen win. No matter what the content of the end-of-year special exam is, I will thoroughly assist them. If I miss this opportunity, I will most likely be the one to disappear.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.203) “If Sakayanagi had followed my instructions, whether that would be before or after I betrayed her in the previous special exam, I was planning to betray Ryūen and join her at the end of the year.”
[says] (p.203) “It's fine if you want to make Ryūen win, but did you propose the same thing to him as you did to Sakayanagi?”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.203) “You mean about recruiting you? Yes, of course. The answer was the same as Sakayanagi's, but there was a condition. If we could defeat Sakayanagi in the end-of-year exam, he would recruit the both of us to his class.”
[says:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.204) “What do you want from me?”
[note] (p.199–204) The whole betrayal arc: the bet; Hashimoto's 55–45 denial; the decisive-factor hunt; Sakayanagi refused to recruit him; he betrays her anyway; the 20M-points safety net he claims Ryūen offered; he expects to disappear if he fails; he smiles nervously.
[rel:hashimoto-masayoshi] (p.199–204) The flashback reveals the entire mechanism — the bet, the class move, the 20M, the timing.
